_note: INVARIANTS rule 4 (state_lint.py, build section 74): nothing is promised until it exists, and nothing exists until it is delivered. This file is the RATCHET for check A1 only -- a Code node that mints `written` or `published` into a stored row without reading the evidence for it. It is EMPTY today: every node that mints a forward state reads something that proves it, and the two defects found while seeding the lint (Publish Check calling the published-row builder for a page that had answered 404, and Mark Case Study Published writing `published` with no gate at all) were fixed rather than baselined. An empty ratchet is not a claim of perfection, so here is what the lint does NOT prove: (1) it proves a node READS the evidence, never that the row it wrote is the row that evidence covers -- `statusCode` in a node says it was built to look, not that it looked at this page; (2) the other five checks (builder, stored, reversal, delivery, verdict) are rules with no baseline at all, so a breach of them fails the build outright and can never be deferred here; (3) the app-side half of B-R1 -- 23 reports that reached the app and no human -- is enforced in app/ (per-company schedule, signed webhook, delivery log, retries), outside any build-time walk of workflow JSON, and no entry here covers it; (4) D10 and R11, pages delivered with placeholders, are held by Content QA's own counts and by harness scenarios, not by this lint: what this lint adds for them is check D, which makes it impossible for a later gate to refuse a draft while the fields the file name, the package banner, meta.json, the callback and the app read still say it passed. A new A1 breach fails the build; adding it here needs a reason and, if it is a defect, a register row in FIX_PLAN.
